citations.locator: EcoCrop_DB.csv row for ScientificName="Daucus carota"; fields KTMP=0, KTMPR=-1
citations.note: KTMP is ECOCROP's 'Killing Temperature' field (named as such in the Notes section of the official tutorial, .research-sources/2026-11-06/ecocrop-tutorial.pdf, p.4: 'Killing Temperature' is one of the described Notes headings). It is the single value closest in meaning to a damage limit (the crop is reported killed, not merely sub-optimal), but the tutorial does not state whether it is a daily-minimum air-temperature reading, an instantaneous low, or a multi-day exposure, nor the growth stage it applies to. KTMPR gives ECOCROP's stated reliability/tolerance range around KTMP, not a second stage. The builder could not re-find the quote in the saved text, so it is not reproduced.

references.summary: Cool-season vegetable grown for its storage root. Established roots and exposed young tissues differ in freezing response. Hot conditions can impair root growth and eating quality. Disease-specific preceding-crop risks matter; an apparently unrelated crop can still host a root pathogen. Compaction, stones and root damage can cause forking; root shape is not a disease diagnosis on its own.
